lookupSnapshot and lookupIterator print an int64_t id with %d, a printf format/type mismatch (undefined behaviour, -Wall warning).

parseOptions reads --cache_size with %ld into the int n, so sscanf writes a long into an int (stack overwrite, truncated size).

fix_subject: Fixed unit test c_test by initializing logger=NULL.
defect: The new member logger_ is never initialized in the DBImpl constructor (crash in c_test), and last_log_ts is a std::atomic that requires a C++0x compiler.

The change adds std::atomic<int64_t> last_log_ts (requiring C++0x, which the build treats as optional) and a StatsLogger* logger_ that the constructor leaves uninitialized, breaking non-C++0x builds and crashing c_test.

fix_subject: fix filename_test
defect: ParseFileName no longer recognizes the legacy LOG.old file name as an info log file.
ParseFileName no longer recognizes the legacy LOG.old info log file name, breaking existing directories and filename_test.

fix_subject: sst_dump: Fix incorrect cmd args parsing
defect: The new --verify_checksum option is matched with strncmp on its length, so arguments with trailing characters such as --verify_checksumAAA are silently accepted instead of being rejected.

The --verify_checksum flag is matched with strncmp over the flag length, so arguments with trailing characters (for example --verify_checksum=false or --verify_checksumXYZ) are silently accepted as enabling verification.

fix_subject: Fix a race condition while processing tasks by background threads.
defect: The change turns the single background thread into a pool of num_threads_ workers but keeps signalling the condition variable only when the queue is empty, so tasks enqueued while the queue is non-empty wake no idle worker and run serially on one thread.
With several background threads, Schedule still signals only when the queue was empty, so tasks enqueued while one worker is busy never wake the other idle workers.

fix_subject: Fix compiler warnings and errors in ldb.c
defect: The new tool prints a uint64_t count with %d (format mismatch, undefined behaviour) and calls exit without including stdlib.h.
The new ldb tool calls exit() without including stdlib.h and prints the uint64_t count with %d, causing a compile error and a printf format mismatch (undefined behaviour).

fix_subject: Fixed issues Valgrind found.
defect: PrintEnv sets compression = (char *)std::string("none").c_str() etc., a pointer into a destroyed temporary that is then printed (use-after-free).
compression is set to std::string(...).c_str() of a temporary, leaving a dangling pointer that is later read by fprintf.

fix_subject: fix test failure
defect: The new DBOpen_Change_NumLevels test opens its database into the fixture member db_, overwriting the fixture's already-open DB without closing it, which leaks that DB (and its lock on dbname_) and makes the test run fail.
The new DBOpen_Change_NumLevels test opens its database into the fixture member db_, overwriting and leaking the DB the fixture already opened (its lock stays held), so the test run fails.

fix_subject: fix complie error
defect: The rewritten assert(descriptor_file_ == NULL || new_descriptor_log) lacks its terminating semicolon, so version_set.cc does not compile.
The modified assert in LogAndApply lacks its terminating semicolon, so version_set.cc does not compile.

fix_subject: Fix a coding error in db_test.cc
defect: MinLevelToCompress returns void, so when no compression is supported the callers still Reopen, write to the null options.compression_per_level and use an uninitialized type.

The extracted helper MinLevelToCompress returns void, so its 'skipping test, compression disabled' return no longer skips the calling tests, which go on with an uninitialised type and a null compression_per_level.

fix_subject: Fix for the weird behaviour encountered by ldb Get where it could read only the second-latest value
defect: DBImplReadOnly::NewIterator dereferences options.snapshot unconditionally, crashing when no snapshot is given, which is the default.
DBImplReadOnly::NewIterator dereferences options.snapshot unconditionally, crashing with the default ReadOptions whose snapshot is null.

WALDumper::DoCommand calls row.clear() to reset the stringstream, which only clears error flags, so every record reprints all previous rows.

fix_subject: Fix LDB dumpwal to print the messages as in the file.
defect: WALDumper calls row.clear() to reset the stringstream, which only clears error flags, so every record reprints all earlier rows.
WALDumper::DoCommand resets the stringstream with row.clear(), which only clears error flags, so every printed row repeats all earlier rows.

fix_subject: Fix compilation error while compiling unit tests with OPT=-g
defect: delete_filter's new parameter is named argv but its new assert uses 'arg', an undeclared identifier, so db_test fails to compile whenever asserts are enabled (OPT=-g).
delete_filter's parameter is named argv but its new assert refers to the undeclared name arg, so debug builds fail to compile.

fix_subject: Fix compilation error introduced by previous commit 7889e094554dc5bba678a0bfa7fb5eca422c34de
defect: The per-edit printing block using verbose and count was inserted into VersionSet::Recover, where neither variable exists, instead of DumpManifest, breaking compilation.
The per-edit printing was added inside Recover(), where neither verbose nor count exists, so version_set.cc no longer compiles.

fix_subject: Fix broken test; some ldb commands can run without a db_
defect: The new early return when db_ is null skips DoCommand for commands that run without a DB (NoDBOpen), breaking them and reduce_levels_test.
The new early return in Run() when db_ is null also skips DoCommand for commands that legitimately run without a DB (NoDBOpen), breaking them and reduce_levels_test.

fix_subject: Fix memory leak for probableWALfiles in db_impl.cc
defect: GetUpdatesSince allocates probableWALFiles with new and returns early without deleting it when no WAL file matches, leaking the vector.
GetUpdatesSince allocates probableWALFiles with raw new and returns early (no matching files, later also on error) without deleting it, leaking the vector.

fix_subject: Fixed off by 1 in tests.
defect: The new BitStream test reads bytes[kNumBytes+1] and bytes[64/8+1] from an array of size kNumBytes+1, an out-of-bounds read.
The new BitStream test reads bytes[kNumBytes+1] and bytes[64/8+1] from a char array of size kNumBytes+1, reading out of bounds.

fix_subject: Fix a bug. Where DestroyDB deletes a non-existant archive directory.
defect: DestroyDB propagates the error from DeleteDir on the archive directory, so it returns failure when no archive directory exists (WAL_ttl_seconds = 0).
DestroyDB now returns the failure of DeleteDir on the archive directory, which does not exist when WAL archiving is off, so DestroyDB reports an error on a normal database.

fix_subject: Fix for the weird behaviour encountered by ldb Get where it could read only the second-latest value
defect: Read-only open now replays the WAL into the memtable (GetMemTable and external_table) instead of writing L0 files, but DBImplReadOnly::Get and NewIterator still read only SST files, so recent writes are missed and ldb sees the second-latest value.

Read-only open now replays the WAL into the in-memory memtable (via the new GetMemTable/external_table) instead of writing L0 files, but read-only Get and NewIterator still read only SST files, so recently written values are invisible.

fix_subject: Fix the warning introduced by auto_roll_logger_test

The new test passes non-literal strings as Log format strings and ignores system()'s return value, triggering -Werror=format-security and -Werror=unused-result build failures.

defect: Zeroing the sequence number calls UpdateInternalKey in place on the key slice owned by the compaction input iterator, which corrupts the merging iterator's ordering.
Compaction zeroes the sequence number in place in the key buffer owned by the input merging iterator, breaking the iterator's ordering assumptions and crashing db_stress.

The replacement condition in HexToString is inverted: it throws for input that starts with 0x and accepts input that does not.

TtlIterator::value() returns a Slice that points into a temporary std::string destroyed at the end of the return statement, so callers read freed memory.

MultiGetSimple writes keys[6] into a vector of size 6, an out-of-bounds write (undefined behaviour caught by valgrind) that also leaves keys[5] empty.

InternalKeyComparator::Name returns c_str() of a temporary std::string, a dangling pointer to freed memory.

The new asserts in RecordTick compare the name-map sizes with ENUM_MAX - 1 although each map lists all ENUM_MAX entries, so every RecordTick fails its assert in debug builds.

The new reseek in FindPrevUserEntry seeks to saved_key_ even when a deletion just cleared saved_key_, seeking to the start of the DB so Prev()/SeekToLast() can return the first key.

fix_subject: Fix SlowdownAmount
defect: SlowdownAmount is declared as (int n, int top, int bottom), but callers pass the lower and upper limits in the opposite order and pass double rate-limit scores that are truncated to int.
SlowdownAmount is declared as (n, top, bottom) with int parameters while callers pass (n, slowdown, stop) and a double score, so top and bottom are swapped and fractional scores are truncated.

AddKey builds Slice prev pointing into entries_ and then calls entries_.append(), which may reallocate, so SamePrefix later reads freed memory (heap use-after-free).

BlockReader now returns a heap-allocated error iterator (instead of nullptr) when no IO is allowed, and InternalGet breaks out of the loop on that Incomplete status without deleting block_iter, leaking the iterator.

defect: Renaming the bytewise comparator to rocksdb.BytewiseComparator makes existing databases (whose MANIFEST records leveldb.BytewiseComparator) fail to open with a comparator mismatch.
Renaming the bytewise comparator to rocksdb.BytewiseComparator changes the persisted comparator name, so existing databases fail to open with a comparator mismatch.

OpenDb allocates options.comparator = new TestKeyComparator() on every call and never frees it, leaking the comparator under valgrind.

fix_subject: [CF] Fix CF bugs in WriteBatch
defect: PutCF, MergeCF and DeleteCF now return InvalidArgument for an unknown column family even during WAL recovery, so replaying a log that references a dropped column family fails recovery.
Writes to an unknown column family now return InvalidArgument and stop WriteBatch::Iterate, so WAL recovery fails on batches that reference a dropped column family, which used to be silently skipped.

fix_subject: Fix Valgrind error introduced by D16515
defect: LogBuffer::AddLogToBuffer is declared variadic, so LogToBuffer cannot forward its va_list and calls AddLogToBuffer(format) with no arguments, making vsnprintf read nonexistent varargs (Valgrind error).

LogBuffer::AddLogToBuffer is declared variadic, so LogToBuffer cannot forward its va_list and calls AddLogToBuffer(format) with no arguments, making vsnprintf read garbage arguments (valgrind errors).

fix_subject: Fix bug in VersionEdit::DebugString()
defect: DebugString appends the uint32_t max_column_family_ with std::string::append instead of AppendNumberTo, which does not produce the number (ill-formed or wrong output).
DebugString appends the uint32_t max_column_family_ with std::string::append instead of converting it to decimal text, producing a wrong (or ill-formed) result.

fix_subject: fix: use the correct edit when comparing log_number
defect: The batch loop computing max_log_number_in_batch reads edit->has_log_number_/edit->log_number_ (the caller's edit) instead of writer->edit, so the largest log number of the batch is wrong.
The batch loop computes max_log_number_in_batch from the outer `edit` instead of each `writer->edit`, so batched flush edits are ignored and log_number_ can be set wrongly.

fix_subject: Fix valgrind error caused by FileMetaData as two level iterator's index block handle
defect: LevelFileNumIterator::value() now exposes the raw bytes of a whole FileMetaData as the index value, so TwoLevelIterator compares uninitialized padding and mutable fields such as refs (valgrind error, possible wrong block reuse).

LevelFileNumIterator::value() exposes the raw bytes of a whole FileMetaData (padding, refs and other uninitialized or changing fields) as the two-level index handle, which TwoLevelIterator compares byte-wise, causing valgrind uninitialized-read errors and spurious mismatches.

fix_subject: Fix MacOS errors
defect: The new log message prints a uint64_t with %lu, a format mismatch that fails the -Werror build on MacOS, where uint64_t is unsigned long long.
The new log statement prints a uint64_t with %lu, a format mismatch that breaks the macOS -Werror build.

fix_subject: Fix the bug in MergeUtil which causes mixing values of different keys.
defect: The new post-loop PartialMergeMulti call passes ikey.user_key, the loop variable that can hold the next user key or stale data, instead of orig_ikey.user_key.

The partial merge moved after the loop calls PartialMergeMulti with ikey.user_key, where ikey is the last parsed key (possibly the next user key) rather than the key being merged (orig_ikey), mixing up keys.

fix_subject: Fix MacOS errors
defect: The new perf test prints uint64_t values with %lu, which fails -Wformat -Werror builds on MacOS.
The new perf test prints uint64_t values with %lu, a format mismatch that breaks the macOS -Werror build of the test.

fix_subject: Fix ASAN issue
defect: The new error message builds list_of_not_found with ", " + cf where cf is an int from std::set<int>, which is pointer arithmetic on a string literal (out-of-bounds read reported by ASAN), and passes a printf-style %s format to Status::InvalidArgument, which does not format it.

The new error-message code does ", " + cf with cf an int from std::set<int>, i.e. pointer arithmetic past a string literal (out-of-bounds read flagged by ASAN), and passes a printf-style %s format to Status::InvalidArgument, which does not format.

fix_subject: Fix compile issues when doing make release
defect: The TEST_ helpers are compiled only under #ifndef NDEBUG, so make release fails to build because code still uses them.
The TEST_ helper functions are compiled only under #ifndef NDEBUG (here and in db_impl.h), so make release, which builds the tests with NDEBUG, fails to compile and link the callers of these helpers.

fix_subject: Fix bugs introduced by D17961
defect: NewIterator and Get call GetTableReaderFromHandle(handle) before checking FindTable's status, so a failed lookup dereferences a null handle (segfault).
NewIterator and Get call GetTableReaderFromHandle(handle) right after FindTable without checking its status, so on failure they dereference a null cache handle and segfault.

fix_subject: Fix bug + formatting
defect: The two overloaded multiGet native methods are both defined under the short JNI name Java_org_rocksdb_RocksDB_multiGet, which does not match the mangled names JNI requires for overloaded natives, so the JVM cannot link them.

Both overloaded native multiGet methods are defined under the short JNI name Java_org_rocksdb_RocksDB_multiGet instead of the mangled names JNI requires for overloaded natives, so the JVM cannot link them.

fix_subject: Fix OSX compile
defect: LevelFileIteratorState is forward-declared as struct but defined as class in version_set.cc, which breaks the OSX clang build (mismatched tags as error).
LevelFileIteratorState is forward-declared as struct but defined as class in version_set.cc, a mismatched tag that breaks the OSX clang build.

fix_subject: bug fix: iteration over ColumnFamilySet needs to be under mutex
defect: The new IsSnapshotSupported iterates the ColumnFamilySet without the DB mutex, called from GetSnapshot before locking and from findEarliestVisibleSnapshot during unlocked compaction, causing segfaults.

The new IsSnapshotSupported() iterates the ColumnFamilySet without holding the DB mutex, called from GetSnapshot before the lock and from findEarliestVisibleSnapshot during compaction with the mutex released, causing a segfault under concurrency.

fix_subject: fix compile warning
defect: uint32_t actual is left uninitialized on the unknown-checksum path, producing a maybe-uninitialized warning that fails the -Werror build.
The new checksum switch leaves `uint32_t actual` uninitialized on the default path, triggering a maybe-uninitialized warning that -Werror turns into a build failure.

fix_subject: Fixed a compile error in util/options_builder.cc
defect: The new file calls std::pow while including only <math.h>, not <cmath>, so it fails to compile where std::pow is not pulled in transitively (clang on Mac).
OptimizeForLevel calls std::pow while only <math.h> is included, which fails to compile on clang/Mac (no member named pow in namespace std).

fix_subject: fix forward iterator bug
defect: UpdateCurrent computes int cmp = Compare(...) > 0, so cmp is only 0 or 1, and assert(cmp != 0) fires whenever the mutable key is smaller than the immutable one.
In UpdateCurrent, int cmp = Compare(...) > 0 stores a boolean, so cmp is never negative and assert(cmp != 0) fires whenever the mutable key is the smaller one.

fix_subject: fix_sst_dump_for_old_sst_format
defect: ReadTableProperties now calls table_properties_.reset(table_properties) even when rocksdb::ReadTableProperties fails, adopting an uninitialized pointer that is later dereferenced or deleted, which segfaults on old-format SST files without properties.

ReadTableProperties now calls table_properties_.reset(table_properties) even when rocksdb::ReadTableProperties failed, taking ownership of an uninitialized pointer, which segfaults sst_dump on old-format files without a properties block.

The new assert(bg_compaction_scheduled_ == 0) in RunManualCompaction does not hold: a concurrent manual compaction can see manual_compaction_ cleared while the finishing background job, having released the mutex (error sleep or PurgeObsoleteFiles), has not yet decremented bg_compaction_scheduled_, so debug builds crash.

defect: SeekToFirst and SeekToLast build the search entry with offset 0 and no search key, so the comparator decodes the batch header as key '' and mis-positions the iterator with non-bytewise comparators.

fix_subject: Fix regression bug of hash index with iterator total order seek (#6328)
defect: LevelIterator stores a null prefix_extractor when total_order_seek is set, so a table reader created during a total-order seek is cached without a prefix extractor and a later prefix seek with a hash index crashes.

fix_subject: Fix an asan warning caused by the recent io_uring change (#6135)
defect: reqs[index].result = reqs[index].scratch builds a Slice from a char* via strlen on an unterminated buffer, which is a heap-buffer-overflow read.
MultiRead assigns reqs[index].result = reqs[index].scratch, building a Slice from a non-terminated char* via strlen and reading past the buffer (ASAN heap-buffer-overflow).

fix_subject: fix build warnnings on MSVC (#6309)
defect: TestCompactRange declares uint32_t pre_hash without an initializer and reads it under a different condition, triggering MSVC's potentially-uninitialized-variable warning that fails the /WX build.
TestCompactRange declares uint32_t pre_hash without an initializer and uses it later under a separate condition, which MSVC reports as potentially uninitialized and fails under /W4 /WX.

fix_subject: Fix a data race related to memtable trimming (#6187)
defect: CheckMemtableFull calls imm->NumFlushed() on the write path without the DB mutex, racing with MemTableList::InstallNewVersion.
CheckMemtableFull calls imm->NumFlushed() on the write path without the DB mutex, racing with MemTableList::InstallNewVersion.

fix_subject: fix build warnnings on MSVC (#6309)
defect: GetOneHotKeyID assigns std::floor results (double) to int64_t, an implicit narrowing conversion that MSVC warns about, breaking the /WX (FAIL_ON_WARNINGS) build of db_stress.
GetOneHotKeyID assigns double results of std::floor to int64_t implicitly, which MSVC flags as a lossy conversion and fails under the default /W4 /WX build.

fix_subject: Fix unused variable in release build
defect: The new GetIntVal computes local `levels` only for an assert, so release (NDEBUG) builds fail with -Werror=unused-variable.
GetIntVal declares a local 'levels' used only in an assert, giving an unused-variable error in release (NDEBUG) builds with -Werror.

fix_subject: Fix test in LITE mode (#6267)
defect: The new test SwitchMemtableRaceWithNewManifest calls SetOptions(), which returns NotSupported in ROCKSDB_LITE, so the test fails in LITE builds.
The new test SwitchMemtableRaceWithNewManifest uses SetOptions, which returns NotSupported in ROCKSDB_LITE, so the test fails in LITE builds.

fix_subject: Fix result slice's address for direct io read (#6672)
defect: When the internal buffer is handed out, the result slice starts at buf.BufferStart() without adding offset_advance, returning the wrong bytes for unaligned direct IO reads.
In direct IO mode with an internal buffer, the result slice starts at buf.BufferStart() without adding offset_advance, so reads at unaligned offsets return the wrong bytes.

fix_subject: Fix bug in MultiRead() coalescing introduced in 4fc216649d (#6446). (#6979)
defect: TryMerge tests std::max(dest_offset, dest_offset) instead of std::max(dest_offset, src_offset), so disjoint read requests are merged into huge reads.
TryMerge tests overlap with std::max(dest_offset, dest_offset) instead of std::max(dest_offset, src_offset), so disjoint requests are merged into huge read requests.

fix_subject: Fix a few bugs in best-efforts recovery (#6824)
defect: CleanupFilesAfterRecovery builds file paths as NormalizePath(path + fname) where the directory paths have no trailing separator, so it computes and deletes wrong paths such as '/db000123.sst'.
CleanupFilesAfterRecovery builds file paths as NormalizePath(path + fname) with no directory separator, so it targets nonexistent paths like "/db000012.sst" when deleting leftover files.

fix_subject: Fix timestamp support for MultiGet (#6748)
defect: The batched MultiGet passes &timestamps[i] to KeyContext even when timestamps is nullptr (the default overload passes nullptr), producing invalid non-null pointers.
The batched multi-CF MultiGet passes &timestamps[i] to KeyContext even when timestamps is nullptr (as the old overload passes), giving bogus non-null pointers that are later written through.

fix_subject: Fix data race to VersionSet::io_status_ (#7034)
defect: The change writes VersionSet::io_status_ inside ProcessManifestWrites and WriteCurrentStateToManifest while the DB mutex is released, racing with SetIOStatusOK() resets and io_status() reads done by other threads under the mutex.

ProcessManifestWrites and WriteCurrentStateToManifest assign the shared VersionSet::io_status_ while the DB mutex is released, racing with other threads that reset it via SetIOStatusOK under the mutex.

fix_subject: Fix hang timer tests on macos (#7208)
defect: Timer computes wake-up times from env_->NowMicros() but waits on a port::CondVar whose TimedWait uses the system clock, so with a mock-time Env the timer misbehaves and its tests hang (on macOS).
Timer computes deadlines from env_->NowMicros() but waits on port::CondVar::TimedWait, which uses the real clock, so with a mock-time Env the timer hangs.

fix_subject: Fix memory corruption caused by new test in options_settable_test (#6676)
defect: The new test fills already-constructed MutableCFOptions objects with special chars and frees them with delete[] on a MutableCFOptions* that was placement-new'ed into a char buffer, without destructors, which corrupts memory (UB).

The new MutableCFOptions round-trip test placement-constructs objects in char buffers, overwrites their live bytes, then calls delete[] on the MutableCFOptions pointers instead of destroying them and freeing the char arrays, causing memory corruption (UB under ASAN).

fix_subject: Fix release build (#6690)
defect: In CompareTimestamp the local ts_sz is used only in asserts, so release (NDEBUG) builds fail with an unused-variable error.
In the new ComparatorWithU64TsImpl::CompareTimestamp the local ts_sz is used only inside asserts, so a release (NDEBUG) build fails with an unused-variable error under -Werror.

fix_subject: Fix unused variable of r in release mode (#6750)
defect: The new alignment check binds 'const FSReadRequest& r' that is used only inside assert(), so release builds get an unused-variable warning, which -Werror turns into a build failure.
MultiRead's direct-IO alignment check binds a reference r that is used only in asserts, an unused-variable error in release builds with -Werror.

fix_subject: Fix a couple of bugs in FaultInjectionTestFS (#6777)
defect: InjectError stores the chosen error type in a local variable, while the new PrintFaultBacktrace prints ctx->type, which is never assigned or initialized.

The change prints ctx->type in PrintFaultBacktrace but stores the chosen error type only in a local variable, so the new ErrorContext::type member is never initialized or set and the reported type is garbage.

fix_subject: Fix valgrind error by init memory region (#6842)
defect: The TamperWithDecompressionOutput callback allocates new char[size + 1] without initializing it and passes it on as block contents, so the test reads uninitialized memory (valgrind error).
The CompressionFailures test replaces block contents with an uninitialized new char[] buffer that is then read and compared, an uninitialized-memory read reported by valgrind.

fix_subject: Fix the memory leak in Env_basic_test (#7017)

fix_subject: Fix TSAN failure for backupable_db_test (#7478)
defect: The CorruptionDuringBackup callback sets a plain bool corrupted from backup worker threads while it is read elsewhere, a data race that TSAN reports.
The added test writes a plain bool `corrupted` from the CopyOrCreateFile sync-point callback, which runs on BackupEngine worker threads, and reads it on the test thread, a data race that TSAN flags.

fix_subject: Fix a minor data race in stats dumping threads initialization (#7151)
defect: The function-static counter stats_dump_threads_started is a plain uint64_t read and incremented under per-DB mutexes, so it races between DB instances.

fix_subject: Fixed the swallowed IOStatus in Compaction Job introduced in PR 7718 (#7838)
defect: The change stops initializing io_s from sub_compact->builder->io_status() and declares a fresh OK io_s later, so a builder IO error is only copied into the plain Status s and never reaches sub_compact->io_status, losing its retryable IO-error classification and disabling auto-resume.

By moving the io_s declaration below the builder Finish, the change stops capturing the table builder's IOStatus in io_s, so sub_compact->io_status is set to OK and a builder write IO error is swallowed (no longer retryable or auto-resumed).

fix_subject: Fix Windows strcmp for Unicode (#8190)
defect: GetChildren calls strcmp on data.cFileName, which is a wchar_t array in the Unicode (UTF8 filenames) Windows build, so that configuration fails to compile.
GetChildren filters . and .. with strcmp on data.cFileName, which is a wide string in Windows Unicode builds, so that configuration fails to compile.

fix_subject: Fix clang analyze for trace replace GetPayload (#8121)
defect: The new GetPayload/IterPayload structs leave cf_id uninitialized, and Replay() reads get_payload.cf_id after DecodeGetPayload, which sets it only if the kGetCFID bit is present (it initializes get_key instead), so this is an uninitialized read.
GetPayload::cf_id and IterPayload::cf_id have no initialiser, and DecodeGetPayload/DecodeIterPayload set them only if the payload map has the CFID bit, so Replay can read an uninitialised cf_id.

fix_subject: Fix race in WriteBufferManager (#9009)
defect: The new write-stall machinery is racy: ShouldStall sets stall_active_ without holding mu_ while EndWriteStall checks queue_.empty() outside the lock and pops front(), and SetBufferSize(0) never wakes stalled writers.

The new write-stall logic sets stall_active_ in ShouldStall without mu_ and EndWriteStall checks queue_.empty() outside the lock before front()/pop_front(), a data race that can crash; SetBufferSize(0) also never releases stalled writers.

fix_subject: Fix test issue in new env_test tests (#8319)
defect: The new io_uring tests install SyncPoint callbacks that capture stack locals by reference and never clear them, so tests run afterwards in the same process trigger stale callbacks and fail.
The new io_uring tests register SyncPoint callbacks that capture locals by reference and never clear them, so later tests in the same process fire stale callbacks on dangling references and fail.

fix_subject: Pin CacheEntryStatsCollector to fix performance bug (#8385)
defect: The CacheEntryStatsCollector is kept only as an ordinary low-priority, unpinned cache entry, so with a full cache it is evicted on release and the expensive full-cache scan is redone for each column family.

GetShared inserts the shared CacheEntryStatsCollector with default low priority and charge 0, so in a full non-strict cache it is evicted on release and every column family triggers a new full cache scan, defeating the one-collector-per-cache guarantee.

fix_subject: Fix Immutable Customizable Serialization (#8457)
defect: The new comparator serializer ignores mutable_options_only, so the immutable comparator is emitted in mutable-option strings and applying them fails with option not changeable.

Making comparator a Customizable (AsCustomRawPtr) whose serializer ignores mutable_options_only causes the immutable comparator to be emitted in mutable-only option strings, which then fail to parse with 'option not changeable'.

fix_subject: Fix an issue with MemTableRepFactory::CreateFromString (#9273)
defect: The new memtable_factory/memtable parse lambdas reset the shared factory whenever CreateFromString returns OK, even when it returns OK with a null factory under ignore_unsupported_options, overwriting the option with null.

The new memtable_factory/memtable parsers reset the shared factory whenever CreateFromString returns OK, but with ignore_unsupported_options it can return OK with a null factory, overwriting the existing factory with null.

fix_subject: Improve fault injection to MultiRead (#8937)
defect: MultiRead injects and counts an error both for individual requests and for the overall return status, so the stress test's injected-error count can exceed the observed failures and report a false positive.

The new MultiRead injects a per-request error and can then inject another error into the overall status, incrementing the injected-error count twice, so db_stress expects more failed keys than it sees and reports a false failure.

fix_subject: Fix LITE mode builds on MacOs (#8981)
defect: The fields sst_file_manager_, mutex_ and error_handler_ were moved out of the non-LITE block but are only used under #ifndef ROCKSDB_LITE, so clang LITE builds fail with -Wunused-private-field -Werror.

The change removed the LITE-specific constructor and made sst_file_manager_, mutex_ and error_handler_ unconditional members used only under #ifndef ROCKSDB_LITE, so LITE builds on macOS fail with -Wunused-private-field -Werror.

fix_subject: Fix FileStorageInfo fields from GetLiveFilesMetaData (#9769)
defect: The new default constructor SstFileMetaData() {} leaves the inherited FileStorageInfo::file_type at its default kTempFile, so objects built by GetLiveFilesMetaData report the wrong file type.

The new empty default constructor SstFileMetaData() leaves the inherited FileStorageInfo fields at their base defaults (file_type kTempFile, empty relative_filename and directory), so GetLiveFilesMetaData reports wrong FileStorageInfo fields.

fix_subject: Fix fstatfs call for compilation on 32 bit systems (#9251)
defect: The new PosixDirectory constructor compares buf.f_type (a signed __fsword_t) with the unsigned BTRFS_SUPER_MAGIC, which fails to compile under -Werror sign-compare on 32-bit systems.

SplitValueIntoChunks allocates chunks with AllocateBlock (the custom MemoryAllocator when one is set) but CacheValueChunk::Free releases them with delete[], a mismatched deallocation that segfaults.

fix_subject: Fix a bug in range scan with merge and deletion with timestamp (#10915)

fix_subject: Fix seg fault in auto_readahead_size during IOError (#11761)
defect: After FindReadAheadSizeUpperBound the index iterator is re-seeked but its validity is never checked before index_iter_->value() is used, so an IO error during the re-seek leaves an invalid iterator and trips an assertion/crash (and the work is redone on the async second pass).

start_time is set only in the timed-delay branch, but delayed can also become true in the stop-wait loop, so time_delayed becomes NowMicros() - 0 and huge bogus stall times are recorded.

fix_subject: Fix wrong padded bytes being used to generate file checksum (#12598)
defect: Pad computes the file checksum over buf_ from pad_start after the loop, but a Flush inside the loop resets the buffer, so the checksum covers the wrong bytes.

The new UpdateFileChecksum call in Pad hashes buf_ from pad_start over actual_pad_bytes after the loop, but if Flush ran during padding the buffer was reset, so the wrong bytes go into the file checksum and verification reports a mismatch.

fix_subject: Fix issue that cause false alarm corruption report (#12626)
defect: saved_seq_for_penul_check_ is set for swapped TimedPut entries but only cleared inside DecideOutputLevel's output_to_penultimate_level_ branch, so a stale value can be consumed by a later entry and cause a false Corruption report.

saved_seq_for_penul_check_ is cleared only when output goes to the penultimate level and the sequence differs, so a stale saved sequence is reused for a later key and causes a false Corruption report.

fix_subject: Fix TSAN-reported data race with uncache_aggressiveness (#12753)
defect: The new non-atomic rep_->uncache_aggressiveness is written by MarkObsolete from several table-cache references in parallel and read in the destructor, which is a data race.
MarkObsolete writes the plain field rep_->uncache_aggressiveness while other table-cache references can mark the same table obsolete and the destructor reads it, a data race.

fix_subject: SyncWAL() before Close() when FLAGS_avoid_flush_during_shutdown=true in crash test (#12900)
defect: The new condition `!FLAGS_avoid_flush_during_shutdown` is inverted: it skips SyncWAL exactly when shutdown does not flush and recovery depends on the WAL, causing false data-loss failures in the crash test.

The new condition !FLAGS_avoid_flush_during_shutdown is inverted: the WAL is left unsynced exactly when shutdown does not flush and reopen relies on the WAL, causing spurious data-loss verification failures.

fix_subject: Fix Unit Test failing from uninit values in CompactionServiceInput (#13080)
defect: The new CompactionServiceInput::options_file_number has no default initializer, so serializing an input that did not set it (as InputSerialization does) reads an uninitialized value (valgrind failure).
The new CompactionServiceInput::options_file_number member has no initializer, so the existing InputSerialization unit test serializes an uninitialized value (valgrind failure).

fix_subject: Fix the handling of PrepareValue failures due to fault injection (#13131)
defect: VerifyIterator treats any PrepareValue() failure as divergence, so read fault injection makes the stress test report false verification failures.

The new PrepareValue() call in VerifyIterator treats any failure as divergence, so a read fault injected by the stress test makes it report a false verification failure (and it reads iter->key() after the failed call has invalidated the iterator).

fix_subject: Fix a valgrind unit test failure (#13137)
defect: MultiGet passes an uninitialized dummy_seq as out_seq to Get, which reads it (*out_seq == kMaxSequenceNumber), a use of an uninitialized value.
WBWIMemTable::MultiGet passes an uninitialized dummy_seq as out_seq to Get, which reads *out_seq == kMaxSequenceNumber, an uninitialized-value read.

fix_subject: Bugfix: Ensure statuses are initialized with OK() in SSTFileReader::MultiGet (#13411)
defect: SstFileReader::MultiGet initializes every status to IOError, so keys the table reader skips (for example filtered by the bloom filter) come back as IOError instead of NotFound; merge operands are also not handled.

The new MultiGet initializes every status to IOError, so keys the table reader never touches (for example excluded by the bloom filter) are returned as IOError instead of NotFound; it also passes no merge operator or merge context.

ExternalTableOptions stores a const FileOptions reference, and this change binds it to a temporary FileOptions(topts.env_options) that dies at the end of the statement, leaving a dangling reference.

fix_subject: crash test and other refactoring (#13704)
defect: AutoSkipCompressorWrapper binds its opts_ member, a const reference, to the caller's CompressionOptions, which can die before the wrapper, giving stack-use-after-return in CompressBlock.
AutoSkipCompressorWrapper stores opts_ as a const reference to a CompressionOptions that can die before the wrapper, causing stack-use-after-return in CompressBlock.

fix_subject: Fix bug in the generation of index and meta blocks when constructing UDI (#13846)
defect: The new wrapper returns early on an Incomplete status from a partitioned internal index (infinite loop), adds the UDI meta block too late to be written, and passes internal keys instead of user keys to the user defined index.

The UDI wrapper returns early on any non-OK status (including Incomplete from a partitioned index, causing an infinite loop), adds its meta block only after the internal index finished so it is never written, and passes internal keys instead of user keys to the user-defined builder.

fix_subject: Fix remote compaction stress test (#13835)
defect: remote_compaction_worker_threads is only reserve()d and then written and read through operator[] beyond size(), which is undefined behaviour (and the capacity()==count assert need not hold).
remote_compaction_worker_threads is only reserve()d and then written and read through operator[] beyond size(), which is undefined behaviour and trips the libstdc++ assertion.

fix_subject: Bug fix in MultiScan and stress test (#13822)
defect: TestMultiScan sets ro.iterate_upper_bound to a loop-local Slice only after the iterator was created from a copy of ro, so the iterator never sees the bound and verification runs with mismatched bounds.

TestMultiScan sets ro.iterate_upper_bound to a loop-local Slice only after the iterator under test was created, so that iterator never gets the bound that VerifyIterator assumes and the pointer dangles across iterations.

fix_subject: Fix multiscan assert failure in stress test (#14077)
defect: The change sets MultiScan use_async_io straight from the flag without checking that the file system supports async IO, hitting an assertion in the block-based table iterator.
